02 — About
Who I Am
ORAN CARMON
The way I think
I don't sell products.
I build the machines that sell them.

For eight years I've walked into the same blank page — a market, a product, and no commercial engine — and built the system that turns intent into predictable revenue.

I think in systems, not heroics. A great seller closes a deal; a great system closes a thousand and compounds while you sleep. My job is to design that system — the ICP, the message, the motion, the metrics, and now the AI layer running underneath all of it.

I've led from both chairs. As a CEO I owned the P&L, the org, the culture. As a builder I still write the sequences, model the pipeline and sit in the discovery calls. That range is deliberate — I refuse to manage what I can't do myself.

What I optimize for
Clarity over noise
Evidence beats opinion. The pipeline doesn't lie — I coach the numbers.
How I operate
Leverage over effort
I'd rather spend a week building the machine than a year running the task.
What I leave behind
Teams that outgrow me
I measure myself by how fast the org stops needing me in the room.
About

First-ever BD hire. No outbound function, no pipeline, no process — and international growth targets across multiple European markets.
Strategy
Defined ICP, segmentation and messaging per market, then designed an AI-powered prospecting infrastructure and an enterprise sales motion built to scale.
Execution
Built the HubSpot CRM architecture end-to-end; wired Apollo, Clay & Hunter with GPT, Claude & Gemini for enrichment and personalization; ran ~6 executive discovery meetings weekly.
Results
€3M+ ARR qualified pipeline, seven enterprise customers closed full-cycle, and payment operations launched in Israel via PayPlus & UPAY.
Lessons
Personalization at scale is an infrastructure problem, not a writing problem. The engine outperforms the effort — every time.

§02 · The Growth Problem
Oran Carmon — Building Revenue Engines
The Growth Problem
Every company wants growth.Few build the commercial systems required to sustain it.
Most organizations don't fail because they lack talented people. They don't fail because they have the wrong CRM. They don't fail because they need more leads. They struggle because growth is treated as a collection of activities instead of a connected commercial system.
Marketing
Generates demand
Sales
Pursues opportunities
Customer Success
Manages relationships
Product
Builds features
Operations
Enables execution
Each function performs well on its own. Yet without alignment, growth becomes unpredictable. The challenge isn't generating more activity — it's building a commercial operating system where strategy, people, execution and technology move in the same direction. Only then does growth become scalable.
The organizations that scale consistently don't rely on extraordinary individuals. They build systems that enable ordinary teams to achieve extraordinary results.
This playbook presents the commercial principles, operating framework and real-world case studies that have shaped the way I build commercial organizations.
Turning Vision Into Commercial Growth

Oran Carmon — Building Revenue Engines
My Commercial Philosophy Awaiting Input
Revenue is engineered,
not chased.
01
Build the system, not the sprint.
Hustle produces a quarter; architecture produces a company. I design the ICP, the motion and the metrics so growth becomes repeatable — never heroic.
02
Evidence is the only currency.
Opinions don't scale — data does. I run commercial orgs on pipeline truth: conversion, velocity and forecast. I coach against the numbers, not the noise.
03
AI is leverage, not decoration.
I don't add AI to look modern. I use it to remove the ceiling on how much intelligence one team can apply — so we punch far above our headcount.
Turning Vision Into Commercial Growth
P.03 — 11

My Commercial Philosophy
A different way to think about commercial growth.
Commercial growth is not created by selling more.It is created by designing better commercial systems.
My Role
I don't build sales departments. I build commercial operating systems. My responsibility is to transform business vision into measurable commercial execution by aligning people, processes, technology and leadership around a common objective: predictable growth.
My Philosophy
Every commercial challenge breaks down into five connected layers — each one feeding the next.
01
Vision
02
Strategy
03
People
04
Systems
05
Execution
→ Outcome
Growth
If one layer is missing, growth becomes inconsistent. When all layers work together, organizations become scalable.
The Builder Mindset
I don't measure success by the number of deals I close. I measure it by the commercial systems that continue creating growth long after they've been built. That mindset has shaped every stage of my career — from leading companies and launching ventures to building AI-powered outbound engines and commercial organizations from the ground up.
Turning Vision Into Commercial Growth
P.03 — 11

# ORAN CARMON — "THE COMMERCIAL BUILDER" — BUILD SPEC (behind-the-scenes)

> Working method: Oran sends page content → I LOG it here (fast, no render). Only at the END do we build + design + render the whole PDF in one pass. Do NOT re-render per page unless he asks.
> Build source: `index.html` (this folder) → Chrome headless `--print-to-pdf` @ 1280×720 → PDF. Fonts base64 in `fonts/fonts.css`. Preview PNGs via PyMuPDF. Output: `C:\Users\Alex\Desktop\ORAN_CARMON_Portfolio.pdf`.

---

## GLOBAL DESIGN SYSTEM
- Format: 1280×720 landscape, one `<section class="page">` per page.
- Palette: matte black `#0D0D0D`; ink `#F4F4F3`; muted `#9E9E98` / `#6C6C67`; lines `#242422` / `#33332F`; **bordeaux accent `#C0435A`** (`--acc`).
- FORBIDDEN: gradients, rounded corners, drop-shadows, glows. Sharp / editorial-brutalist only.
- Fonts: **Archivo** (display/titles, 700–900), **Fraunces** (serif — big editorial statements & italic accents), **Space Mono** (labels, marginalia, page numbers), **Inter** (body).
- Signature chrome on content pages: 4 corner brackets (bordeaux, thin); optional left "spine" (thin line, bordeaux tick top); top header mono — left `§NN · Section Name`, right `Oran Carmon — Building Revenue Engines`; bottom footer mono — left running label, right `P.NN — 11`.
- **Exceptions:** Cover = book title page (no chrome). Page 2 = bare statement (only page number bottom-right). Page 4 = NO right-header, NO signature line, NO My Role box.
- **Vary composition every page** — no two consecutive pages share the same skeleton. Use mature graphic elements: arrows (▼ / →), node dots, connecting lines, hairline ledgers, corner brackets.
- **Unified vocabulary** (his framing): Commercial System · Operating Model · Growth Engine · Go-to-Market · Commercial Infrastructure · Revenue Architecture · Commercial Execution · Scalable Growth. Avoid raw "Sales/Deals/Pipeline" in framing; keep verbatim where he deliberately contrasts (e.g. "I don't build sales departments").
- **My Role box: REMOVED — do not use.**
- Total pages: **11**. Footer total reads `— 11`.

## PAGE ORDER (11)
1. Cover · 2. Statement · 3. My Commercial Philosophy · 4. XTIX (part 1) · 5. XTIX (part 2) · 6. Oasis · 7. Medcoin · 8. AI Growth Engine · 9. Leadership Principles · 10. Results · 11. Let's Build Together.

---

- Title (Archivo 800, caps): **THE COMMERCIAL BUILDER**
- Sub (Fraunces italic, bordeaux): *From Vision to Measurable Growth*
- small bordeaux rule

## PAGE 2 — STATEMENT  (STATUS: DONE) — bare page, two red Fraunces lines centered, only "P.02 — 11" bottom-right
- "Most companies don't need better salespeople."
- "They need better commercial decisions."

## PAGE 3 — MY COMMERCIAL PHILOSOPHY  (STATUS: DONE) — vertical 8-node flow (left, boxes + ▼) aligned to principles (right); signature line at bottom
- Title (Archivo): **Every Business Is Different.** / *The Principles of Growth Are Not.* (2nd line bordeaux)
- Flow nodes + principles:
  1. VISION — Define where the business is going.
  2. BUSINESS UNDERSTANDING — Understand the business before improving it.
  3. MARKET UNDERSTANDING — Understand the customer before creating the message.
  4. COMMERCIAL ARCHITECTURE — Build the commercial engine before scaling it.
  5. PEOPLE & LEADERSHIP — Create ownership, not dependency.
  6. EXECUTION — Turn strategy into consistent execution.
  7. MEASUREMENT — Measure decisions, not assumptions.
  8. CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT — Learn faster than the market evolves.
- Signature Principle: *First build a system that works. Then build a business that scales.*

## PAGE 4 — XTIX (PART 1)  (STATUS: DONE) — 2×2 "cards/zones"; NO right-header, NO signature, NO My Role
- Eyebrow: Case Study 01 · Title (Archivo): Building a Commercial Function From Zero · Meta: XTIX · FinTech SaaS · Early-Stage Startup
- **01 The Situation:** "When I joined XTIX, the company had a strong vision and product — but no commercial infrastructure to support scalable growth." → *Commercial Reality:* No CRM · No Business Development function · No sales methodology · No outbound process · No pipeline management · No KPI framework · No reporting structure
- **02 My Mission:** "Design and build a commercial operating system capable of supporting predictable business growth — starting with the Israeli market and later expanding globally."
- **03 My Approach:** "Rather than launching outbound immediately, I focused on understanding the business first. The first phase included:" → Business & product analysis · Market research · Competitive analysis · ICP definition · Customer segmentation · Commercial positioning → *Only then did execution begin.*
- **04 What I Built:** ✓ Commercial Strategy · HubSpot CRM Infrastructure · Business Development Process · Sales Pipeline · ICP Framework · Outbound Sequences · KPI Framework · Forecasting Structure · Reporting Dashboards · AI-Powered Outbound Engine

## PAGE 5 — XTIX (PART 2): Execution → Evidence → Lessons  (STATUS: DONE) — 3 columns + bottom band (Looking Back + quote)
- Eyebrow: Case Study 01 · XTIX — Commercial Execution · Title: Execution → Evidence → Lessons
- **Commercial Execution:** "Once the commercial foundation was established, execution shifted from planning to building a repeatable growth engine." + "The focus was no longer on individual sales activities — it was on creating a commercial operating system that learns, improves and scales."
- **Key Initiatives:** Building & managing outbound campaigns from scratch · ICP-specific messaging & sales sequences · HubSpot as the commercial operating system · KPI dashboards & reporting structure · AI-powered commercial intelligence platform · International commercial expansion · Repeatable forecasting & pipeline management
- **Evidence of Execution** (table, Area → Outcome): Pipeline → €3M+ ARR pipeline managed · Meetings → ~6 qualified meetings/week · Opportunities → ~20 new opportunities/week · Outbound → Reply rate ~20% · Outbound → Conversion 7–8% · Inbound → Conversion 50%+ · Markets → Europe, US & global · CRM → Commercial infrastructure built in HubSpot · AI → Internal AI sales-intelligence platform
- **What Made the Difference:** objective was to improve commercial decision-making (not automate sales) · every outbound sequence built around customer context · every KPI existed to improve decisions · every workflow reduced manual effort while raising quality · technology = amplifier, not the strategy.
- **Lessons Learned (5):** 01 Commercial infrastructure before commercial scale · 02 AI doesn't replace commercial thinking, it accelerates it · 03 A CRM is not a database, it's the operating system of a commercial org · 04 Market understanding beats copywriting for messaging · 05 The strongest systems improve themselves via continuous feedback.
- **Looking Back box:** "If I were rebuilding XTIX today, I would invest earlier in product differentiation and enterprise-focused go-to-market execution. Building the commercial engine was the right decision — building stronger market differentiation even earlier would have accelerated growth further."
- **Quote:** "Technology scales execution. Understanding scales decisions."

# CONTENT BIBLE — single source of truth (extracted verbatim from ORAN_CARMON_Portfolio.pdf)
# RULE: every word below must appear in both deliverables. Nothing invented beyond dossier microcopy tokens.
# Old doc = 12 pages. New doc = 13 (CASE FILES divider inserted as P.04). Mapping: old N ≥ 4 → new N+1.

## NEW P.01 — COVER (old p1) ✓ BUILT
THE COMMERCIAL BUILDER / From Vision to Measurable Growth / EXECUTIVE CASEBOOK / BY ORAN CARMON
Quote: "If you connect to the vision, you'll always know where you're going."
Tagline (footer): A PRACTICAL GUIDE TO BUILDING COMMERCIAL ORGANIZATIONS THAT SCALE  ← replace current footer-left chips

## NEW P.02 — STATEMENT (old p2) ✓ BUILT
Most companies don't need better salespeople. / They need better commercial decisions.

## NEW P.03 — PHILOSOPHY (old p3) ✓ BUILT
Title: Every Business Is Different. The Principles of Growth Are Not.
8 steps: Vision / Business Understanding / Market Understanding / Commercial Architecture / People & Leadership / Execution / Measurement / Continuous Improvement (+ one-line descs as built)
Signature Principle: First build a system that works. Then build a business that scales.

## NEW P.04 — THE CASE FILES divider ✓ BUILT (new page, approved)

## NEW P.05 — XTIX PT.1 (old p4)  [EMBER folder]
Eyebrow: CASE STUDY 01 · Title: Building a Commercial Function From Zero
Meta: XTIX · FINTECH SAAS · EARLY-STAGE STARTUP
01 THE SITUATION: "When I joined XTIX, the company had a strong vision and product — but no commercial infrastructure to support scalable growth."
COMMERCIAL REALITY (missing-at-intake ⊖): No CRM / No Business Development function / No sales methodology / No outbound process / No pipeline management / No KPI framework / No reporting structure
02 MY MISSION: "Design and build a commercial operating system capable of supporting predictable business growth — starting with the Israeli market and later expanding globally."
03 MY APPROACH: "Rather than launching outbound immediately, I focused on understanding the business first. The first phase included:" → Business & product analysis / Market research / Competitive analysis / ICP definition / Customer segmentation / Commercial positioning → "Only then did execution begin."
04 WHAT I BUILT (✓×10): Commercial Strategy / HubSpot CRM Infrastructure / Business Development Process / Sales Pipeline / ICP Framework / Outbound Sequences / KPI Framework / Forecasting Structure / Reporting Dashboards / AI-Powered Outbound Engine

## NEW P.06 — XTIX EVIDENCE (old p5)  [EMBER]
Title: Evidence — From Infrastructure to Execution
PERFORMANCE: Pipeline Managed €3M+ ARR · Qualified Meetings ~6 per week · New Opportunities ~20 per week · Outbound Reply Rate ~20% · Outbound Conversion 7–8% · Inbound Conversion 50%+
OPERATIONS (✓×6): Built the company's commercial reporting structure / Implemented forecasting methodology / Designed KPI framework / Established pipeline management / Standardized outbound methodology / Supported international commercial expansion
TECHNOLOGY: "Designed & implemented an internal AI-powered commercial intelligence platform that:" Researched prospects automatically / Imported & enriched leads from commercial databases / Generated personalized outreach per prospect's business / Automated commercial sequences / Continuously improved through feedback & knowledge → "Purpose: Improve commercial decision-making while increasing execution capacity."
REFLECTION — IF I WERE REBUILDING XTIX TODAY: Differentiate the product earlier against competitors / Accelerate enterprise positioning / Invest in strategic partnerships sooner / Expand the AI platform even earlier / Build the Israeli operation in parallel with global activity
LESSON: "Commercial growth doesn't begin when the first campaign is launched. It begins when the commercial system becomes repeatable."

## NEW P.07 — OASIS PT.1 (old p6)  [BRASS folder]
Eyebrow: CASE STUDY 02 · Title: Building Leaders, Not Just Sales Teams
Meta: OASIS · CEO · CONSTRUCTION & SMART BUILDING SOLUTIONS
01 THE SITUATION: "As CEO, my responsibility extended far beyond sales. The objective wasn't simply to increase revenue — it was to build a profitable, scalable commercial organization capable of supporting the company's long-term vision."
02 MY RESPONSIBILITIES (×9): Recruiting & building the sales team / Defining commercial strategy / Pricing model development / KPI design / Sales methodology / Forecasting / Commercial reviews / Cross-functional leadership / Profitability management
03 COMMERCIAL SYSTEM BUILT (✓×8): Recruited & onboarded the entire sales team / Built the pricing model from scratch / Designed the commercial process / Implemented KPI framework / Created sales playbooks & onboarding / Established weekly business reviews / Built forecasting methodology / Created cross-functional collaboration
04 LEADERSHIP MODEL (×7): Weekly coaching sessions / Monthly 1:1 performance reviews / Quarterly business reviews / Live deal reviews / Commercial coaching / Cross-functional collaboration / Clear ownership & accountability
SIGNATURE INSIGHT: "High-performing sales teams aren't built by pressure. They're built by clarity."

## NEW P.08 — OASIS EVIDENCE (old p7)  [BRASS]
Title: Evidence — Commercial Results
COMMERCIAL LEADERSHIP (×6): Recruited an entire sales team / Led a team of 5–6 sales professionals / Conducted weekly coaching sessions / Established KPI-driven management / Built onboarding documentation / Standardized commercial processes
BUSINESS PERFORMANCE (×6): Largest deal closed: ₪2M / Built pricing strategy from zero / Introduced profitability-based pricing / Defined company-wide commercial KPIs / Improved cross-department collaboration / Created structured commercial reporting
CROSS-FUNCTIONAL LEADERSHIP — "Worked closely with:" (✓×6): Operations / Production / Customer Success / Finance / Marketing / Technical Teams
REFLECTION — LOOKING BACK: "The biggest lesson I learned as CEO wasn't about selling — it was about leadership. The more I tried to manage every function myself, the less scalable the organization became. Real leadership begins when leaders build systems that let others succeed without depending on them."
LESSON: "Organizations don't scale because leaders work harder. They scale because leaders create clarity, ownership and trust."

## NEW P.09 — EVENTER (old p8)  [ICE folder]
Eyebrow: CASE STUDY 03 · Title: Aligning Commercial Execution Across Teams
Meta: EVENTER · SAAS · EVENT MANAGEMENT PLATFORM
THE SITUATION: "Eventer already had an existing commercial operation. Unlike previous roles, the objective wasn't to build a department from scratch — it was to improve execution, strengthen collaboration between departments and identify new commercial growth opportunities."
MY ROLE: "I worked across multiple business functions to improve commercial performance by connecting business strategy with day-to-day execution."
KEY CONTRIBUTIONS (✓×7): Managed & coached Business Development team members / Participated in recruiting commercial talent / Improved commercial processes / Introduced new business initiatives / Worked closely with Product, Marketing, Finance & R&D / Brought customer feedback directly into product discussions / Helped improve commercial alignment across the organization
CROSS-FUNCTIONAL IMPACT: "Rather than focusing only on Business Development, I worked closely with multiple departments to ensure customer insights translated into business decisions. Commercial growth became a shared organizational responsibility — not just a sales target."
WHAT I LEARNED: "Leadership doesn't always require authority. Some of the biggest organizational changes happen through influence, collaboration and better decision-making."
SIGNATURE INSIGHT: "Commercial growth accelerates when every department understands the customer — not only Sales."

## NEW P.10 — MEDCOIN (old p9)  [WHITE paper folder — inverted page]
Eyebrow: FOUNDER CASE STUDY · Title: Building a Business From Vision
Meta: MEDCOIN TEKNOLOJI · CRYPTO FINTECH · FOUNDER
THE VISION: "Create a compliant, scalable cryptocurrency ATM business serving the European market through secure, accessible digital financial services."
THE CHALLENGE: "Building a company from zero meant making every strategic decision — from business model and partnerships to compliance, operations and commercialization."
WHAT WE BUILT (✓×9): Founded the company from scratch / Defined the business model / Built the commercial strategy / Established strategic partnerships / Raised external investment / Deployed cryptocurrency ATMs across Europe / Built operational & regulatory processes / Managed financial-service providers & international vendors / Designed the customer journey & user experience
BUSINESS OUTCOMES (×6): MARKETS Europe · BUSINESS MODEL Crypto ATM network · INVESTMENT External investment raised · REVENUE Hundreds of thousands of € · INFRASTRUCTURE Operational ATM network deployed · TEAM Founder-led operation
WHAT I LEARNED: "Being a founder changes how you think. Every commercial decision affects operations. Every operational decision affects profitability. Every strategic decision affects survival. Leading a company taught me that commercial leadership is ultimately business leadership."
LESSON: "Founders don't manage functions. They align the entire business around one vision."

## NEW P.11 — LEADERSHIP (old p10)
Title: Building People. Building Systems. Building Accountability.
Intro: "I believe leadership is not measured by how many people report to you — it is measured by how many people become better because of you. My role is to create clarity, ownership and an environment where people consistently perform at their best."
LEADERSHIP PRINCIPLES (×5):
01 Build Trust Before Performance — "People perform better when expectations are clear and trust is earned."
02 Coach Before You Judge — "Every performance issue deserves investigation first — understand the process, review the data, listen first, coach second, decide last."
03 Create Ownership — "People shouldn't execute tasks. They should own outcomes."
04 Decisions Based on Facts — "KPIs don't replace leadership — they improve it. Every coaching session begins with evidence, not assumptions."
05 Great Managers Solve Today's Problems. Great Leaders Build Tomorrow's System. — "My objective was never to close one more deal — it was to build an organization that produces consistent results without depending on one individual."
LEADERSHIP TOOLKIT (✓×10): Hiring & Recruitment / Onboarding Programs / Weekly Team Meetings / Monthly 1:1 Reviews / Quarterly Performance Reviews / KPI Design / Coaching / Sales Methodology / Performance Improvement Plans / Cross-functional Leadership
SIGNATURE PRINCIPLE: "Leadership is not about creating better employees. It's about creating people who no longer depend on you."

## NEW P.12 — COMMERCIAL TECHNOLOGY & AI (old p11)
Title: How I use technology to improve commercial decisions.

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
# Tone lift: charcoal ladder up 1-2 steps (toward matte charcoal-gray),
# matching dark-ink text lifted the same way. Applies to BOTH files.
import io

SWAPS = [
    # neutral ladder
    ("#131417", "#191A1F"),                # bg + dark ink-on-tab
    ("rgba(19,20,23,", "rgba(25,26,31,"),  # dark-ink alphas
    ("#1A1B1F", "#202127"),                # card
    ("#1F2126", "#25262D"),                # card2
    ("#2E3036", "#33353C"),                # grid
    ("#46494F", "#4B4E55"),                # grid2
    ("#101114", "#16171C"),                # drawer face / lip bar
    ("#0B0C0E", "#111217"),                # drawer inner shadow strip
    ("#0F1013", "#15161B"),                # redact bars (dark)
    ("#26282D", "#2C2D33"),                # handle / light redacts
    ("#5A5B60", "#606167"),                # dim text nudged up for contrast
]
# site relight tints (acts5 LIGHTS) — same delta (+6,+6,+8)
TINTS = [
    ("'#14201B'", "'#1A2621'"),
    ("'#1B1815'", "'#211E1D'"),
    ("'#141920'", "'#1A1F28'"),
    ("'#17181B'", "'#1D1E23'"),
]

def apply(path, tints):
    s = io.open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    total = 0
    for a, b in SWAPS:
        n = s.count(a)
        s = s.replace(a, b)
        total += n
        print("  %-22s -> %-12s x%d" % (a, b, n))
    if tints:
        for a, b in TINTS:
            n = s.count(a)
            s = s.replace(a, b)
            print("  %-22s -> %-12s x%d" % (a, b, n))
    io.open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s)
    print(path, "total neutral swaps:", total)
    return s

print("== casebook.html ==")
apply("casebook.html", tints=False)
print("== site.html ==")
s = apply("site.html", tints=True)
head = ('<!doctype html>\n<html lang="en">\n<head>\n<meta charset="utf-8">\n'
        '<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1">\n'
        '<meta name="color-scheme" content="dark">\n</head>\n<body>\n')
io.open("site_standalone.html", "w", encoding="utf-8").write(head + s + "\n</body>\n</html>")
print("standalone rebuilt")
